title: Delivery ontology
description: The delivery layer of the layered ontology in DD-11 of AI-Assisted Work: epics and stories as profiles of the work layer's WorkItem and Activity, the typed and sized deliverable, the quarterly work plan, the capability increment and its steps on the definition ladder (the stage grid), capacity and resourcing, deliverable types, products and feature requests, as the quarter-planning skill reads them (skills/quarter-planning/references/data-contract.md). It builds on the work layer, pkg:generic/dermot-obrien/ai-assisted-work/work-ontology, by $ref and allOf and redefines nothing in it. A product, registered so consumers can use it and raise feature requests against it, belongs here; what a work item produces is the work layer's Deliverable. Rows of a CSV register are described with every value as it may be read: text, or a number where the column is numeric.
$comment: Additive: the programme, milestone, gate, commitment and slip types DD-11 places in this layer are still defined in AI-Assisted Architecture's base ontology, and move here with its next major version.

Approval.description: An approval stage. The stages are the workspace's approvalStages, least advanced first; the default is draft, sized, validated, approved, and the last is commitment.

Stage.description: A stage of the workspace's definition ladder, such as R2: one step a capability climbs, least defined first. Called a rung before 1.1.0.

Rung.description: Deprecated: the old name of Stage. Read, never written.

NumberLike.description: A number, or its text as a CSV cell holds it.

Flow.description: The movement an epic commits to for one flow of its lane, from one stage to another.

EpicPlanning.description: The planning fields an epic carries, whichever store holds it.

budget_points.description: Capacity the epic may spend, derived from the quarter's resourcing. Set by planning, never estimated.

planned_points.description: The sum of its deliverables' sizes. Compared with the budget, never reconciled to it.

lane.description: The capability area the epic advances. One per epic.

home.description: The epic's hand-written folder, by name, under the epicsDir binding.

site_route.description: The route of the epic's own page on the published site, relative to its root.

SizedDeliverable.description: A work item's deliverable, typed from the deliverable register and sized in points. Extends the work layer's Deliverable.

points.description: Overrides the type's base points. Omitted means the register's base_story_points.

actual_points.description: What it took, recorded at quarter close to recalibrate the register.

stage.description: The one stage this deliverable is for. A type can be produced at many stages; a planned deliverable names the one it moves its capability towards. Omitted, its type's stage is used when the type has only one. This places it in a cell of the stage grid.

stage_reason.description: Why it is for this stage, where that is a judgement worth recording.

Epic.description: An epic in a work-item folder's progress.yaml: a WorkItem whose work_item_level is epic, with the planning fields added. planning_period is the quarter's label.

Story.description: A story: an Activity of an epic, with the route of its page and the feature requests it builds part of.

request_ids.description: The feature requests this story builds part of. A request is assigned to its epic in the request register; stories cite it here, separately.

RegisteredDeliverable.description: A deliverable of an epic record in work_item.yaml: the work layer's Deliverable, typed by deliverable_id and owned by a stakeholder.

deliverable_id.description: The deliverable type, an id in the deliverable register.

EpicRecord.description: An epic as the planning model's work_item.yaml holds it, under the top-level work_item list. Where the same epic is also a work-item folder, this record wins.

quarter.description: The quarter label it is planned in, as quarterLabel builds it.

StoryRecord.description: A story as the planning model's activity.yaml holds it, under the top-level activity list.

WorkPlan.description: A plan committing a period's work, under work_plan.yaml's top-level work_plan list.

work_item_ids.description: The epics and other work the plan commits to.

DeliverableType.description: A row of the deliverable register: a kind of product an epic can name, with its base size.

stages.description: Every stage this type can be produced at: a deliverable type is one to many with stages. A list, or one text with stages separated by semicolons. Empty means any stage.

rung.description: Deprecated: the one stage a type evidenced before 1.1.0. Read as stages.

Product.description: A row of the product register: something registered so consumers can use it and raise feature requests against it, offered by a platform and owned by a team.

owner.description: Read where there is no team.

WsjfFactor.description: A WSJF factor on the scale 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 20, or empty where not yet scored.

FeatureRequest.description: A row of the feature-request register: a request raised against one product, ranked by WSJF, and taken on by at most one epic.

product.description: The product's id in the product register.

epic.description: The epic taking it on, empty until one does.

status.description: One of the workspace's requestStatuses; the default is analyzing, backlog, implementing, validating, releasing, done, rejected.

CalendarPeriod.description: A row of the quarter's calendar.

PlanningAssumption.description: A row of the planning basis: one assumption, its value and the reasoning behind it.

Allocation.description: A row of the resourcing register: one person's share of their allocation given to one piece of work.

CapabilityIncrement.description: One lane's planned movement in one period: a row of the stage grid. The lane is a capability or capability area, the columns are the ladder's stages, and the increment is what the period's epics in that lane will move and how far. It is planned once per lane per period and joins the means (the epics) to the ends (the criteria that say what must become true).

lane.description: The capability or capability area the increment moves.

period.description: The planning period's label, as epics record it.

flows.description: The movement committed for each flow of the lane in scope this period.

epic_ids.description: The epics that carry the increment.

criterion_ids.description: What must be true for the increment to be done.

outcomes.description: What others deliver that the increment counts on, such as a capability put into service by a product team.

IncrementOutcome.description: Something an increment counts on that the planning team does not deliver itself, such as a build put into service by a product team, with the stage it shows the capability at.

status.description: Such as already delivered, or delivered this period.

product.description: The product it is offered as, when there is one.

IncrementStep.description: One cell of the stage grid: what one capability increment delivers towards one stage. Derived, never stored: its deliverables are those of the increment's epics that are for this stage. It answers 'what are we doing this period to move this capability to this stage'.

LadderStage.description: A row of the definition ladder: one stage, least defined first. Called LadderRung before 1.1.0.

builds.description: What is built to reach this stage, as a list or as one text with items separated by semicolons. Shown on the stage grid's column.

band.description: The phase this stage belongs to, such as Define, Design, Build or In service. Consecutive stages in the same band and with the same mover are drawn as one band under the stage grid's columns.

moved_by.description: Who moves a capability to this stage, such as architecture, delivery or run. The planning team's limit, drawn as a line on the stage grid, is the last stage it moves.

consumable.description: Whether a capability at this stage can be consumed. The first consumable stage is flagged on the stage grid.

LadderRung.description: Deprecated: the old name of LadderStage.
